A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSafe work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained material and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original harmfulness-detection experiments, component ablations, and WildGuardTest robustness results in Tables 1–2, with case studies in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds medical-safety, jailbreak edge-case, and specific-policy evaluations in Appendix C.4, Tables 6–8.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbone, policy-guided reasoning, format and accuracy rewards, GRPO training without supervised warm-up, and dynamic policy conditioning remain unchanged. Appendix C.4 evaluates existing capabilities without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: v3 substantially expands evaluation coverage through MedSafetyBench, CARES base and adversarial cases, selected JailbreakBench and JailJudge prompts, and synthetic compliance tests for fine-grained financial, legal, and medical policies. The original training sources and general-safety benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds ShieldGemma-9B-adaptive, providing a policy-conditioned comparator alongside ordinary ShieldGemma. Table 1 retains its six baselines; the new appendix comparisons otherwise use existing guard-model families and GPT-4o.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces substantive evaluation designs: filtering out prompts refused by GPT-4o, comparing identical moderation instructions on the remaining 17 JailbreakBench and 432 JailJudge prompts, and testing balanced synthetic sets of 40 prompts per policy domain. Medical tests use corresponding ethical guidelines, and Table 1 adds weighted aggregate metrics. Existing training budgets and original test splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 substantially extends robustness analysis beyond WildGuardTest through medical-domain shift tests with policy adaptation, selected difficult jailbreak cases, and fine-grained policy-compliance tests. The original reasoning/RL ablations and Appendix E case studies are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly states that main RSafe experiments are run three times and averaged. This discloses a run count rather than establishing increased replication. No seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Existing numerical cells in Tables 1–2 are unchanged, but v3 adds weighted summaries, adaptive ShieldGemma results, and Tables 6–8. New results include MedSafetyBench accuracy of 0.804 for RSafe-adaptive versus 0.881 for GPT-4o, and JailbreakBench accuracy of 0.706 for RSafe versus 0.882 for GPT-4o. Specific-policy accuracy reaches 0.975–1.000 for RSafe-adaptive. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same safeguard definitions, reward equations, relative advantage, and GRPO objective. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about data-efficient reasoning-based safeguards, competitive detection, generalization, policy adaptation, and interpretability. The additional experiments support existing claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 adds interpretations of medical-domain performance drops and attributes the larger JailbreakBench gap partly to its small sample. It also qualifies near-perfect synthetic-policy results as primarily demonstrating instruction following rather than nuanced reasoning. The original backbone-capacity and user-policy limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds data-preparation information, including GPT-4o refusal filtering and balanced synthetic policy-compliance construction. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, prompt templates, and repository link are unchanged. Exact medical guidelines and synthetic generation prompts are not supplied.

R1.justification: v3 retains the original references and adds 13 works, including medical and jailbreak benchmark sources and additional safety-alignment research. Related-work prose remains largely unchanged. Section 4.2 also newly acknowledges ShieldGemma's support for user-specified policies, refining the comparison with prior safeguards.

P1.justification: v3 adds Appendix C.4 with three subsections, an acknowledgement, and a NeurIPS checklist, and updates the conference footer. The existing main narrative, method explanations, prompts, and case studies remain largely verbatim, with limited cross-reference changes.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains weighted-average columns, Table 2 gains an adaptive-baseline row, and three new result tables appear in Appendix C.4. The original prompt tables are renumbered from 6–8 to 9–11. Figures 1–3 are unchanged; remaining layout differences mainly reflect text reflow.

improvement.justification: The adaptive ShieldGemma comparison and targeted Appendix C.4 tests make the central adaptivity claim better tested than v1's WildGuardTest evidence alone. Reporting weaker edge-case performance and qualifying the synthetic-policy results also improves assessment of applicability. The gain is limited by selected small samples, absent uncertainty estimates, and overbroad medical-superiority wording: Table 6 shows unadapted RSafe trailing LlamaGuard3 on MedSafetyBench and CARES base. Overall, the added evidence provides a useful but limited quality improvement.
